correctness.rationale: For p<q, tau(p^2q^2)=9 and sigma factors as Phi_3(p)Phi_3(q). Exact valuations nu_3(Phi_3(r)) in {0,1}, the order-three condition for other prime divisors, and the inequality Phi_3(p)/3 < p^2 < q^2 force p=13, q=61 after p=2 and p=3 are handled; Phi_3(61)=3*13*97 excludes that pair. All primes and positive exponents k are covered without computational extrapolation.

evidence: Pollack–Pomerance 2012 §5.2 gives a global upper counting bound for superharmonic integers, not an exact two-prime exponent exclusion.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A theorem on prime-perfect or prime-deficient integers need not cover this family: sigma(p^2q^2) can contain an extra prime 3 supplied by tau(n), even though 3 need not divide n. The even family 2^a p excludes a different exponent profile. An unseen result specifically allowing the 3 could dominate and is recorded as a risk.

value.rationale: The square of a semiprime is a natural complete exponent profile within the unresolved problem of odd and two-prime-support superharmonic numbers. The result excludes an entire infinite nonsquarefree layer, not a finite numerical range; the forcing of precisely three intermediate pairs illustrates a reusable small-prime cyclotomic-support obstruction. The claim is restricted to this structural boundary and does not assert a general solution.
